adversarial-nli-anli.title: Human-and-Model-in-the-Loop Adversarial NLI (ANLI)
adversarial-nli-anli.decision: Collect hard NLI examples by having humans write hypotheses that fool a target model, producing a benchmark that resists saturation (a "moving target").

failure_modes.description: Examples are selected to fool a specific model, so the distribution is adversarial, not natural — strong for stress-testing, not representative of organic NLI (the recurring adversarial-collection caveat).
failure_modes.caught_by: UNGUARDED (rounds re-target as models improve, but each round is still model-shaped)

failure_modes.description: Adversarial hypotheses can be genuinely ambiguous, so even verifiers may disagree on the gold label. (Inferred.)

quality_gates.checks: other annotators confirm the intended label
only model-fooling examples are kept

cost_profile.throughput: moderate — fooling the model takes annotator effort + retries
cost_profile.bottleneck: annotator creativity + the in-the-loop model serving
cost_profile.human_cost: standard crowd; low welfare risk

audio-transcription-commonvoice.title: Crowdsourced Read-Speech Corpus with Vote Validation (Common Voice)
audio-transcription-commonvoice.decision: Produce validated <audio, transcript> pairs at massive multilingual scale to train/eval ASR, where validity = the spoken audio matches the displayed sentence.

failure_modes.description: Extreme coverage variance — English 780 validated hours vs Abkhaz <1; low-resource languages have almost no speaker diversity (Slovenian 3 unique train speakers, Irish 6), so ASR can't generalize there.
failure_modes.caught_by: UNGUARDED (reported as a limitation, not solved in-corpus)

failure_modes.description: Same speaker in train + test would inflate ASR scores (model recognizes the voice, not the language).
Early voting mechanism had bugs; some clips received >3 votes, resolved by simple majority. An implementation defect, not a systematic data-quality signature.
Binary up/down conflates "wrong words" with "heavy accent / bad audio"; no rubric separates them. Source does not report this.
Self-selected volunteers + Wikipedia sentences bias speaker and domain distribution away from deployment. Source notes optional demographics but does NOT report representativeness bias.
Validity is pure crowd consensus with no expert/gold reference; no ground truth on the validators. Not reported.

quality_gates.checks: only clean in-language sentences become recordable
a clip is valid only on majority agreement
no speaker in more than one of train/dev/test
dev/test sized for a target confidence / margin

cost_profile.throughput: massive, fully crowdsourced; near-zero marginal cost per clip
cost_profile.bottleneck: validator attention in low-resource languages (too few contributors to reach 2 votes)
cost_profile.human_cost: distributed across volunteers; scarce resource = contributors per language

benchmark-bigbench.title: Community-Contributed Eval Benchmark (BIG-bench)
benchmark-bigbench.distinctive: An eval benchmark built by the COMMUNITY — 204 tasks contributed by 450 authors across 132 institutions, peer-reviewed and merged on a rolling basis; dynamic and extensible. Coverage emerges bottom-up from whatever researchers care to contribute, not top-down from a coverage plan.
benchmark-bigbench.decision: Build a broad, extensible capability benchmark by soliciting, reviewing, and merging tasks contributed by the research community.

failure_modes.description: Tasks reflect contributors' interests, not a systematic map of capabilities; coverage is uneven and bottom-up.
Task quality varies; some contributed tasks were later critiqued as ill-posed (the 'common sense' subset debate).
Some skills are over-covered (popular topics), rare capabilities under-covered. (Inferred.)

quality_gates.checks: reviewers vet each task before merge

cost_profile.throughput: community-scale, bursty; near-zero central labeling cost
cost_profile.bottleneck: review capacity + sustaining contributions
cost_profile.human_cost: volunteer researchers

clinical-annotation-guidelines.title: Clinical Text Annotation with Iterative Guidelines + Adjudication
clinical-annotation-guidelines.decision: Produce a gold-standard annotated clinical corpus (entities/events) by iteratively refining guidelines until expert annotators agree, then adjudicating the rest.

failure_modes.description: Clinical language is ambiguous; early IAA is low until guidelines are iteratively refined on the edge cases ("continually updated during adjudication; new rules created to arrive at one consistent label").
Physician annotator + adjudicator time is scarce and expensive; the gold corpus is slow to build.

quality_gates.checks: discuss disagreements, add edge-case rules, re-annotate until IAA stable
two annotators + a third-expert adjudicator

cost_profile.throughput: low — expert-bound, multiple iterations
cost_profile.bottleneck: physician annotation + adjudication + guideline iterations
cost_profile.human_cost: scarce medical experts; the iterative process is the cost

clinical-chexpert-labeler.title: Image Labels from Reports via Rule-Based NLP (CheXpert)
clinical-chexpert-labeler.distinctive: Don't label the images at all — run the free-text radiology REPORTS through a rule-based NLP labeler (mention-extraction → classification → aggregation, with phrase lists hand-curated by board-certified radiologists + NegBio negation/uncertainty) to emit 14 observation labels per X-ray. Keeps an explicit UNCERTAIN class instead of collapsing it.
clinical-chexpert-labeler.decision: Generate large-scale structured image labels cheaply by extracting observations from the paired radiology reports with a rule-based NLP labeler.

failure_modes.description: Labels reflect the REPORT's language, not the image directly; report-image mismatch + uncertain wording propagate as label noise.
Rule-based extraction errors have no per-image human check at scale. (Inferred.)
failure_modes.caught_by: UNGUARDED (CheXbert later added expert-validated BERT labeling)

failure_modes.description: Radiology language is hedged; many findings are genuinely uncertain, kept explicit rather than resolved.

quality_gates.checks: keep 'uncertain' as a class, not forced to pos/neg
expert-built mention patterns

cost_profile.throughput: very high — automated text labeling, no image annotation
cost_profile.bottleneck: curating + maintaining the phrase rules
cost_profile.human_cost: small (radiologists curate rules once); no per-image labeling

code-humaneval.title: Execution-Verified Code-Generation Eval Set (HumanEval)
code-humaneval.decision: Build an eval set (164 problems) measuring whether generated code is FUNCTIONALLY correct — graded by running unit tests, not by text similarity.

failure_modes.description: Models train on "a large fraction of GitHub, which already contains solutions" (>10 public repos with Codeforces solutions) — a scraped eval would be contaminated. The hand-writing gate exists to prevent this.
~7.7 unit tests/problem may not fully specify correctness — a weak suite can pass a subtly wrong solution. NOTE: the paper does NOT analyze test coverage/adequacy, so this is inferred, not reported.
failure_modes.caught_by: UNGUARDED (mutation testing / coverage analysis would help)

failure_modes.description: Problems are "easy interview" difficulty and may not represent real software tasks. The paper notes the scope but does not claim representativeness; this concern is inferred.

quality_gates.checks: problems written from scratch, not copied from sources already on GitHub
functional correctness by running tests, not match metrics like BLEU

cost_profile.throughput: small set (164) authored once; execution scales cheaply
cost_profile.bottleneck: expert authoring of correct problems + comprehensive tests
cost_profile.human_cost: skilled authors up front; near-zero at grading time (execution is automated)

code-swebench.title: Harvested GitHub Issues, Execution-Verified (SWE-bench)
code-swebench.decision: Measure whether a model can resolve a real GitHub issue by generating a patch, verified by running the repository's tests (fail-to-pass + pass-to-pass).

failure_modes.description: ~32.67% of "resolved" instances had the solution outlined directly in the issue report/comments (SWE-Bench+), and 94% of issues predate the LLM knowledge cutoff (contamination risk) — apparent skill is partly leakage/memorization.
failure_modes.caught_by: UNGUARDED (SWE-Bench+ adds SolutionLeakDetector + post-cutoff issues → 0% leakage)

failure_modes.description: ~31% of passing patches used WEAK tests ("incorrect, incomplete, or applied to different files" changes passed). Filtering weak tests + leakage drops SWE-Agent+GPT-4 resolution 12.47%→3.97% (Full), 22.4%→10.0% (Verified).
Issues skew to popular Python repos of a certain era; may not represent software work broadly. (Inferred.)

quality_gates.checks: patch must flip fail-to-pass tests and not break pass-to-pass

cost_profile.throughput: large (auto-harvested); execution is automated
cost_profile.bottleneck: building reliable per-repo execution environments; test adequacy
cost_profile.human_cost: near-zero labeling (harvested); engineering to containerize repos

content-moderation-abuse.title: Abusive-Language / Hate-Speech Annotation
content-moderation-abuse.decision: Label text as abusive/hateful (binary or by taxonomy) to train moderation classifiers, where "abuse" is an inherently contested, context-dependent judgment.

failure_modes.description: Dataset DECAY: ID-only releases lose content (Mathew et al. counterspeech lost >60% in 12 months), and the class distribution + qualitative nature shift over time (overt abuse is removed faster than covert).
A complex taxonomy "is only suitable for ML if there are enough data points in each category and if annotators can consistently distinguish between them" — rich schemas become non-implementable.
Low IAA is endemic — abuse is "inherently subjective, contextual, political"; irony/sarcasm/intent are hard; some guidelines just say label "according to your opinion."
failure_modes.caught_by: edge-case guidelines + majority vote (raise the floor, don't close it)

failure_modes.description: Creator homogeneity — 70% of sexist / 99% of racist tweets in the Waseem-Hovy set come from 1-2 users — makes "user-level metadata artificially highly predictive of abuse" (the model learns the author).
Keyword oversampling drives racial bias; Twitter over-represented; far-right oversampled vs far-left; event-window sampling kills generalisability.
Datasets are "radically unrepresentative" of real (<1%) abuse prevalence, so eval ≠ deployment.

quality_gates.checks: combine ≥3 annotators; vote proportion as soft severity
report κ/α (often low for non-binary taxonomies)
clear guidelines WITH examples that "only just cross the line"

cost_profile.throughput: varies (crowd cheap/fast; expert slow)
cost_profile.bottleneck: "high-quality data requires volumes of painstaking labour and deep expertise"; ethical crowd pay ≈ expert cost
cost_profile.human_cost: WELFARE-CRITICAL — authors stress the "harmful and potentially triggering effects of annotating online abuse" and urge emotional/practical support + fair pay. (Welfare captured here per the cost_profile convention.)

content-moderation-welfare-ops.title: Commercial Content Moderation (Decisions + Moderator Welfare)
content-moderation-welfare-ops.decision: Have employed moderators decide remove/keep (+ violation category) on user content at scale — labels that both enforce policy and train moderation models — while sustaining the moderators doing the work.

failure_modes.description: Policy changes frequently and moderator judgment shifts under fatigue, so "the bar" moves over time.
Policy can't cover every edge case moderators face; ambiguous calls under time pressure.
Burnout / secondary-trauma degrade consistency (rushed or numbed decisions). (Inferred from the welfare findings.)

quality_gates.checks: exposure limits, breaks, content-masking, counseling, time-based pay
sample audits + appeal overturns

cost_profile.throughput: very high (continuous queues)
cost_profile.bottleneck: sustainable moderator capacity
cost_profile.human_cost: SEVERE & WELFARE-CRITICAL — ~100k commercial moderators face repeated graphic exposure with documented PTSD symptoms, secondary traumatic stress, compassion fatigue, anxiety/depression (Steiger et al. 2021). Wellness interventions (psychological + technological, e.g. content masking) are part of the workflow, not optional.

corpus-ingestion.title: Corpus Ingestion — Source Documents to Curated Workflow Cards
corpus-ingestion.decision: Turn raw source documents into validated workflow cards (and candidate patterns) decomposed into the schema, so the corpus can scale beyond hand-authoring without losing the provenance-over-volume guarantee.

failure_modes.description: THE central risk — the extractor invents a plausible failure mode the source never reported, and it enters the corpus as if observed. Kills the provenance-over-volume guarantee.
failure_modes.caught_by: REPORTED-vs-INFERRED tagging + human audit + gold-set check

failure_modes.description: The extractor launders its own priors about how workflows "should" work as if extracted from the source (the Pop Problem, in ingestion form).
You ingest the easy-to-find sources (arXiv, HF), so the corpus over-represents well-documented academic workflows and under-represents messy real-world vendor practice.
failure_modes.caught_by: coverage routing (partial — UNGUARDED for the published-vs-practiced bias itself; needs deliberate non-academic source pulls)

failure_modes.description: The corpus bloats with near-duplicate cards that look like coverage but aren't (many papers describe the same multi-annotator + adjudication skeleton).
If one model family extracts AND is later used in the tool, its framing dominates the corpus.
Rare task structures (red_team, 3D, transcription) are rare in sources too, so they stay uncovered unless deliberately sought.

quality_gates.checks: extracted cards are compared against the hand-built seed cards as a gold standard
every failure mode is tagged by source-evidence; only REPORTED ones make a war-story card
a second model family re-extracts; framing divergence is flagged
near-duplicate skeletons become exemplars, not new cards
thin signature/modality cells drive the next source pull

cost_profile.throughput: high on extraction (cheap model passes); gated by human audit
cost_profile.bottleneck: the human curator (audit + promotion + dedup) — small but high-skill, exactly like synthetic-with-audit
cost_profile.human_cost: build/maintain the gold set (the seed cards) + audit a stratified sample per batch

critique-criticgpt.title: Critique-Rationale Collection via Bug Tampering (CriticGPT)
critique-criticgpt.decision: Collect critique-quality data — natural-language feedback that catches bugs in code — to train a critic model (RLHF) that helps humans evaluate model outputs.

failure_modes.description: Critics HALLUCINATE bugs that "could mislead humans into making mistakes"; the absolute rate of nitpicks and hallucinations "is still quite high." Without the planted-bug gold you can't separate a real catch from a confabulated one. (Direct echo of Bryan's CoT-faithfulness / pop-problem confabulation findings.)
failure_modes.caught_by: tamper-to-ground-truth (only for the planted bug; UNGUARDED for novel hallucinations)

failure_modes.description: "The distribution of inserted bugs is quite different from the distribution of natural LLM errors" — tampered bugs are harder/more severe than natural ones, so the gold-creation method itself biases the data.
failure_modes.caught_by: UNGUARDED (some unmodified data included to mitigate)

failure_modes.description: Contractors "often disagree when they compare two critiques on overall quality" (low agreement, subjective); agreement improves substantially WITH a reference bug description.
failure_modes.caught_by: tamper-to-ground-truth (the planted bug anchors the subjective judgment)

quality_gates.checks: a known reference bug exists, so "did the critique catch it?" is checkable
rate comprehensiveness / nitpicks / hallucinations / helpfulness

cost_profile.throughput: scales with contractor tampering + rating
cost_profile.bottleneck: skilled contractors who can insert subtle bugs and judge critiques
cost_profile.human_cost: skilled; reviewing buggy code is cognitively heavy (lower welfare risk than abuse content)

crowd-aggregation-dawid-skene.title: Probabilistic Label Aggregation (Dawid-Skene)
crowd-aggregation-dawid-skene.distinctive: Don't take a naive majority vote — jointly ESTIMATE each annotator's CONFUSION MATRIX and the true labels via EM, then weight annotators by their inferred reliability. The classical principled answer to 'how do I combine noisy, unequally-skilled annotators?' (the constructive counterpart to the MTurk quality crisis).
crowd-aggregation-dawid-skene.decision: Recover the most likely true labels from multiple noisy annotators by modeling each annotator's error pattern and down-weighting unreliable ones.

failure_modes.description: Needs enough overlap per annotator to estimate a confusion matrix; sparse labeling → unreliable estimates. (Inferred.)
Assumes conditional independence of annotators; correlated/colluding workers violate it and bias the estimate. (Inferred.)
True labels are estimated, not observed; without any gold, systematic shared error is invisible. (Inferred.)
failure_modes.caught_by: UNGUARDED (seed with a few gold items)

quality_gates.checks: weight annotators by inferred confusion matrices, not equally

cost_profile.throughput: cheap to run; needs label redundancy (the cost is the overlap)
cost_profile.bottleneck: redundant labeling to support the estimation
cost_profile.human_cost: standard crowd

crowd-quality-mturk.title: Crowd Data Collection Under the MTurk Quality Crisis
crowd-quality-mturk.decision: Collect labels/survey responses from an anonymous paid crowd, reliably enough to use — despite workers who optimize pay over quality.

failure_modes.description: Workers "click through surveys as fast as possible," give nonsense free-text, fail reverse-coded items, attenuating effects ~10-30%. Crucially, "common attention checks alone are insufficient" — the gate is in an arms race with the gaming. (2nd gaming exemplar, a domain distinct from red-team template-farming.)
Much fraud comes from "non-US respondents who use VPNs to circumvent location requirements" — the sample isn't the intended population, and the location gate is bypassed.
Speed-clickers default to easy/midpoint responses, compressing signal. (Plausible; not the papers' focus.)

quality_gates.checks: trap items + reverse-coded questions catch inattentive/gaming workers
restrict to qualified US workers

cost_profile.throughput: high/cheap — the appeal that created the crisis
cost_profile.bottleneck: post-hoc quality screening + replacement of bad responses
cost_profile.human_cost: low welfare risk; the cost is silent data corruption

data-quality-cleanlab.title: Find NATURAL Label Errors via Confident Learning (CleanLab)
data-quality-cleanlab.distinctive: Find the label errors ALREADY in a dataset (no planting). Confident learning uses a model's predicted class probabilities + per-class confidence thresholds to flag likely-mislabeled items, then HUMANS validate the flagged subset (~51% of flags confirmed real). Found ~3.4% errors across 10 famous test sets (even MNIST).
data-quality-cleanlab.decision: Surface and correct the mislabeled items already present in a dataset, by ranking label-error candidates with confident learning and human-validating the top flags.

failure_modes.description: Confident learning leans on the model's own probabilities — if the model shares the systematic error, it won't flag it (a blind spot it can't see).
There's no a-priori ground truth; only ~51% of algorithmic flags are confirmed errors, so human validation is mandatory.
Errors the model is confident about get flagged; errors it's also uncertain on slip through. (Inferred.)

quality_gates.checks: humans confirm flagged candidates (only ~51% are real)
use a model that didn't train on the item (ideally a different family)

cost_profile.throughput: high — algorithmic flagging; humans only validate the top candidates
cost_profile.bottleneck: human validation of flagged subset + getting good out-of-sample probabilities
cost_profile.human_cost: small, targeted validation

datasheets-documentation.title: Dataset Documentation & Provenance (Datasheets for Datasets)
datasheets-documentation.distinctive: A META workflow: instead of producing labels, the dataset CREATOR fills a standardized datasheet — 57 questions across 7 categories (motivation, composition, collection process, preprocessing/cleaning/labeling, uses, distribution, maintenance). By analogy to electronics datasheets, it makes a dataset's provenance + intended use + limitations explicit, so consumers can judge fitness. The accountability layer over every other recipe.
datasheets-documentation.decision: Make a dataset's provenance, composition, intended uses, and limitations explicit and inspectable by having its creator answer a standardized question set.

failure_modes.description: Without a standard, datasets ship undocumented; even with one, questions get answered inconsistently/incompletely.
It's self-reported by the creator — blind spots and biases in collection may go unrecorded. (Inferred.)
Creators can rationalize or omit unflattering provenance. (Inferred.)

quality_gates.checks: every dataset answers the same provenance/use/limitation questions

cost_profile.throughput: one datasheet per dataset
cost_profile.bottleneck: creator diligence
cost_profile.human_cost: creator time; high leverage (documents everyone else's work)

demonstration-instructgpt.title: Screened-Contractor Demonstrations + Comparisons (InstructGPT)
demonstration-instructgpt.decision: Produce demonstrations of desired behavior + preference comparisons to align a model via SFT + RLHF, reflecting the labelers' (and researchers') preferences.

failure_modes.description: Labelers are mostly English-speaking US/SE-Asia, college-educated; authors state the model aligns to THEIR labelers' and researchers' preferences, "not representative of the full spectrum" of users.
failure_modes.caught_by: held-out labeler generalization (tests overfit, does not broaden representation)

failure_modes.description: Inter-labeler agreement ~73%; value judgments depend on labeler identity/background; persistent disagreement.
failure_modes.caught_by: screening + IAA (raises floor, doesn't close it)

failure_modes.description: "Most comparisons labeled by 1 contractor for cost reasons" — no redundancy to even measure per-item disagreement.

quality_gates.checks: select labelers by sensitivity-test performance + agreement-with-researchers
unscreened raters who produced no training data confirm the model isn't overfit to training labelers
report IAA as a health metric

cost_profile.throughput: tens of thousands of demos/comparisons from ~40 contractors
cost_profile.bottleneck: screening + the close researcher-labeler collaboration
cost_profile.human_cost: skilled contractors; single-labeling chosen to control cost

detector-planted-mislabels.title: Planted-Mislabel Injection for Bad-Data Detection
detector-planted-mislabels.decision: Measure how well a bad-data detector catches mislabeled training items, by planting KNOWN mislabels and checking how many it recovers — so detector quality is itself verifiable.

failure_modes.description: Planted mislabels may not match the distribution of NATURAL mislabels (the exact caveat CriticGPT reports for tampered bugs) — high recovery on planted errors can overstate real-world catch rate.
failure_modes.caught_by: UNGUARDED (mitigate by planting realistic error types + auditing natural cases too)

failure_modes.description: Without the planted key there's no ground truth on the detector's flags — you can't tell a true catch from a false positive. The planted key is exactly what anchors detector evaluation.
If the planting heuristic and the detector share assumptions, the detector "catches" its own planting style. (Inferred.)

quality_gates.checks: a recorded ground-truth flip exists, so detector recall is directly measurable
don't evaluate the detector only with its own family/heuristic
block a batch from training when flagged-bad rate exceeds the bar

cost_profile.throughput: high — planting + detection automated; the public demo is stdlib/deterministic
cost_profile.bottleneck: designing realistic planted-error types; auditing natural errors to validate the proxy
cost_profile.human_cost: low; the skill is in making planted errors resemble real ones

eval-chatbot-arena.title: Open Crowd Pairwise Battles + LLM-Judge (Chatbot Arena / MT-Bench)
eval-chatbot-arena.lineage: lmsys / Chatbot Arena + MT-Bench (Zheng et al. 2023)
eval-chatbot-arena.distinctive: Preference collection for EVALUATION (ranking models), not training. OPEN, in-the-wild crowd: anonymous A-vs-B battles where anyone votes which response is better → Elo ratings. Paired with MT-Bench, an LLM-as-judge (GPT-4) validated at ~80% agreement with human experts (≈ human-human agreement). Surfaces the judge biases directly: position, verbosity, self-enhancement.
eval-chatbot-arena.decision: Rank models by collecting pairwise human preferences (open crowd battles → Elo) and validate an LLM judge against human agreement so it can scale the evaluation.

failure_modes.description: Position bias — judges (human or LLM) favor whichever response is shown first; mitigated by randomizing position.
Verbosity bias — longer answers are preferred regardless of substance (length confounded with quality).
Self-enhancement bias — an LLM judge rates its own family's outputs higher.
Open crowd voters self-select; the live prompt mix isn't a controlled distribution. (Inferred.)

quality_gates.checks: hide model identity; randomize which side is A
validate the LLM judge against human-human agreement (~80%)
watch for the judge favoring its own family's outputs

cost_profile.throughput: very high — open crowd + LLM judge scale cheaply
cost_profile.bottleneck: the expert-pair gold baseline + bias mitigation
cost_profile.human_cost: open volunteers + a small expert-pair gold set

image-bbox-adjudicated.title: Object Bounding-Box Labeling with Redundancy + Adjudication
image-bbox-adjudicated.decision: Produce tight, consistent object boxes (class + extent) to train a detector, reliable enough that box quality isn't the ceiling on model performance.

failure_modes.description: "Where exactly does the box edge go" on occluded/truncated objects is undefined, so IoU agreement is low and labels aren't learnable. The cure is guideline examples for the hard cases, not more annotators.
A single adjudicator on every low-agreement image throttles the whole campaign.
Rare objects are scarce in a random sample, so the detector never learns them.
Boxes look great on easy daytime scenes while night/occluded scenes — the deployment tail — are under-labeled.

quality_gates.checks: N independent boxes must agree above an IoU threshold
a senior pass resolves the hard cases
seeded known-answer images score each annotator
deliberate intake of under-represented classes

cost_profile.throughput: thousands of images/day; scales with annotator pool
cost_profile.bottleneck: adjudication of low-IoU images
cost_profile.human_cost: N-way redundancy multiplies per-image cost; adjudicators are scarce

image-classification-imagenet.title: Crowdsourced Image Classification against an Ontology (ImageNet)
image-classification-imagenet.distinctive: Verify candidate web images against a WordNet ONTOLOGY ('is this a <synset>?'), with a DYNAMIC vote budget — at least ~10 Turker votes per image, and harder synsets keep collecting votes until a confidence threshold is met. Scaled to 12M images / 22k categories at ~99.7% reported precision.
image-classification-imagenet.decision: Build a massive labeled image set by crowd-verifying candidate images against WordNet synsets, spending more votes where agreement is low.

failure_modes.description: Some synsets are visually ambiguous / overlap; harder categories need many more votes to settle.
Candidates come from web image search, biasing toward canonical/photogenic instances. (Inferred.)
WordNet synsets vary enormously in available web images. (Inferred.)

quality_gates.checks: collect votes until a confidence threshold (more for ambiguous synsets)
≥~10 independent votes per image

cost_profile.throughput: massive crowd; cost scales with the dynamic vote budget
cost_profile.bottleneck: vote volume on ambiguous synsets
cost_profile.human_cost: distributed crowd; low welfare risk

instruction-openassistant.title: Instruction Data — Community Conversation Trees (OpenAssistant)
instruction-openassistant.distinctive: COMMUNITY-sourced — 13,500+ volunteers build conversation TREES (prompt root → branching replies), write both prompter and assistant turns, and RANK assistant replies by preference. Multilingual (35 languages, 161k messages, 461k quality ratings). GAMIFIED: points + leaderboards drive contribution; content-moderation + spam filtering guard quality.
instruction-openassistant.decision: Build an open, multilingual assistant-conversation corpus + preference rankings from a volunteer community, for instruction tuning and alignment.

failure_modes.description: Points + leaderboards can incentivize volume over quality; spam/abuse must be filtered.
Self-selected volunteers skew the topic/language/style distribution away from any given deployment. (Inferred.)
Volunteer 'quality' judgments are subjective and variably skilled. (Inferred.)

quality_gates.checks: multiple volunteers rate/rank each message
remove abusive/spam contributions

cost_profile.throughput: community-scale, near-zero marginal cost; bursty (volunteer-driven)
cost_profile.bottleneck: sustaining volunteer engagement + moderation
cost_profile.human_cost: volunteers; low pay/welfare cost but engagement is the constraint

instruction-self-instruct.title: Instruction Data — Synthetic Bootstrap (Self-Instruct / Alpaca)
instruction-self-instruct.lineage: self-instruct (Wang et al. 2022); applied by Alpaca
instruction-self-instruct.distinctive: SYNTHETIC — start from a tiny human seed (~175 tasks), prompt the LM (8-shot) to GENERATE new instructions + input/output instances, FILTER them (dedupe + quality), add back to the pool, and iterate. Almost no human labeling; instruction data is bootstrapped from the model's own generations.
instruction-self-instruct.decision: Generate a large, diverse instruction-tuning set with minimal human effort by bootstrapping off the model's own generations from a small seed pool.

failure_modes.description: The generator's biases + errors propagate into the data; the student inherits the teacher's blind spots.
failure_modes.caught_by: UNGUARDED (cross-family generation / human audit would help)

failure_modes.description: Diversity is bounded by the seed + the model; whole task types the model can't imagine stay absent.
failure_modes.caught_by: dedupe (spreads coverage; doesn't add what's missing)

failure_modes.description: Generated instances have no human ground-truth check beyond filtering heuristics. (Inferred.)

quality_gates.checks: remove near-duplicate / low-quality generated instructions

cost_profile.throughput: very high — synthetic generation is cheap
cost_profile.bottleneck: generation API cost + filtering quality
cost_profile.human_cost: tiny (only the ~175-task seed)

judge-eval-study.title: LLM-as-Judge Evaluation Study
judge-eval-study.decision: Produce a defensible score (or ranking) of model outputs on some quality dimension, reliable enough to make a claim about how models differ.

failure_modes.description: A judge rates outputs from its own model family higher. Observed directly in Bryan's program: a GPT-4o judge showed +0.74 self-affinity while a Claude judge ran self-critical at -0.26. If generator and judge share a family, you measure self-preference, not quality.
Raw judge scores are trusted with no human ground truth, so you cannot tell whether the judge tracks quality at all. The fix that recurs across the program is a small blind human-rated gold set.
Panel scores drift upward and compress at the top; everything reads as "good." Worse when scoring is relative and unanchored to exemplars.
The first item seen sets the bar for the rest; item order leaks into scores. A real confound that forced a v2 redesign in one study.
A confident model-ranking claim drawn from too few cells. Tight nulls and chance-level adjacencies hide in small n.

quality_gates.checks: rubric and analysis plan are frozen before any scores are seen
judge and humans cannot see model identity or position
a second judge from a different model family scores the same cells
model judge agreement with blind human raters on a sample
enough cells/reps for the effect being claimed

cost_profile.throughput: hundreds of cells per run; cheap if the judge is a model
cost_profile.bottleneck: the human gold sample (slowest, but the gate everything else leans on)
cost_profile.human_cost: rubric authoring up front + blind gold scoring of a sample

ner-conll2003.title: Expert Span Annotation for NER (CoNLL-2003)
ner-conll2003.distinctive: Careful EXPERT span annotation — humans mark named-entity spans (PER / LOC / ORG / MISC) over newswire under explicit guidelines, with inter-annotator agreement tracked (well-run NER reaches ~0.95). The canonical human-gold supervised-NER standard — the opposite of distant supervision's noisy KB-derived labels.
ner-conll2003.decision: Produce gold named-entity spans by having annotators mark entity boundaries + types under shared guidelines, reconciling disagreements.

failure_modes.description: Entity boundaries + types are ambiguous (spans of tokens make the unit count itself unclear); needs guidelines + adjudication to reach high IAA.
Newswire-only → poor transfer to other genres/domains. (Inferred.)

quality_gates.checks: shared boundary/type rules; track κ
a senior pass resolves disagreements

cost_profile.throughput: moderate — careful human span labeling
cost_profile.bottleneck: expert annotation + adjudication
cost_profile.human_cost: skilled annotators; low welfare risk

nli-snli-artifacts.title: NLI Data by Crowd Hypothesis-Writing (SNLI) — the Artifacts Cautionary Tale
nli-snli-artifacts.distinctive: Crowdworkers are shown a premise + a target label and asked to WRITE a hypothesis that entails / contradicts / is neutral to it. Cheap and huge — but the writing protocol leaves label-predictive fingerprints: a hypothesis-ONLY model hits ~67% on SNLI / ~53% on MNLI vs 33% chance. A canonical lesson in how a generation protocol leaks the label.
nli-snli-artifacts.decision: Build a large NLI corpus cheaply by having crowdworkers write hypotheses for given premise+label — and learn why that protocol bakes in artifacts.

failure_modes.description: The crowdsourcing protocol leaves clues — negation/specificity/length correlate with label — so a hypothesis-only model reaches ~67% (SNLI) / ~53% (MNLI) vs 33% chance. Models 'pass' by exploiting artifacts.
failure_modes.caught_by: partial-input baseline (diagnostic; doesn't remove the artifacts)

failure_modes.description: Specific lexical phenomena (e.g. explicit negation → contradiction) are confounded with the label.
failure_modes.caught_by: UNGUARDED (ANLI's model-in-the-loop collection was the field's structural fix)

failure_modes.description: Premises are image captions; the hypothesis space reflects worker habits, not natural inference. (Inferred.)

quality_gates.checks: estimate label agreement on a sample
can a model predict the label from the hypothesis ALONE? if yes, there's leakage

cost_profile.throughput: very high — cheap crowd writing
cost_profile.bottleneck: validation subset
cost_profile.human_cost: standard crowd; low welfare risk — the cost here is silent (artifacts), not human

pointcloud-detection-nuscenes.title: Multi-Sensor 3D Bounding-Box Annotation (nuScenes)
pointcloud-detection-nuscenes.decision: Produce accurate 3D bounding boxes (class + attributes + velocity) over fused LiDAR/camera/radar at 2Hz keyframes, to train/eval autonomous-driving perception.

failure_modes.description: "Severe class imbalance with a ratio of 1:10k for the least and most common class" (vs 1:36 in KITTI); 13 of 23 classes dropped for <10k instances; importance sampling needed.
failure_modes.caught_by: scene selection emphasizing rare classes (partial); UNGUARDED at train time

failure_modes.description: Data only from Boston + Singapore — "more research is required on generalizing to different countries, lighting, previously unseen object types." Keyframe-only (2Hz) leaves intermediate frames unlabeled.

Label reliability degrades with distance/occlusion/night (as few as 1 lidar point at range; visibility <40% boxes "may be unreliable") — the box is ambiguous to place when the sensor barely sees the object.

quality_gates.checks: each annotation passes multiple review rounds
annotate only objects with ≥1 lidar/radar point

cost_profile.throughput: 1.4M boxes / 40k keyframes; large expert effort
cost_profile.bottleneck: expert 3D annotation + multi-round validation; manual face/plate labeling "prohibitively expensive"
cost_profile.human_cost: skilled 3D annotators; cost/timeline not disclosed

pointcloud-segmentation-semantickitti.title: Dense Point-Cloud Segmentation over Superimposed Scans (SemanticKITTI)
pointcloud-segmentation-semantickitti.distinctive: Dense PER-POINT semantic labels (25 classes, 4.5B points) — not boxes. Annotators SUPERIMPOSE a sequence of LiDAR scans into one consistent cloud (SLAM poses), tile into 100×100m regions, label once with a custom OpenGL brush/polygon tool, and propagate — then a two-pass verification enforces temporal+spatial consistency.
pointcloud-segmentation-semantickitti.decision: Produce dense, temporally-consistent point-wise semantic labels for LiDAR sequences by labeling aggregated scans once and propagating across frames.

failure_modes.description: Dense point labeling is extremely slow/laborious even with superposition + tooling.
failure_modes.caught_by: scan-aggregation (label once, propagate) — mitigates, doesn't remove

failure_modes.description: Class + boundary calls on sparse points (moving objects leave traces) are ambiguous. (Inferred.)
KITTI urban-driving sequences; limited geographic/sensor diversity. (Inferred.)

quality_gates.checks: label the aggregated cloud, not each frame, for consistency
temporal + spatial consistency review

cost_profile.throughput: low — dense labeling is the canonical AV annotation bottleneck
cost_profile.bottleneck: per-point human labeling + verification
cost_profile.human_cost: skilled annotators + custom tooling

preference-anthropic-hh.title: Preference Collection — Anthropic HH-RLHF
preference-anthropic-hh.distinctive: Helpful and harmless collected as SEPARATE axes (not one blended 'better'); ONLINE-iterated — preference data is periodically re-collected with the latest model so the reward model stays in distribution. Crowdworkers pick the more-helpful (helpfulness task) or the more-harmful (red-team / harmlessness task) of two model responses.
preference-anthropic-hh.decision: Collect chosen/rejected response pairs to train SEPARATE helpfulness and harmlessness reward models, kept current via online iteration.

failure_modes.description: A static reward model drifts out of distribution as the policy improves; online iterated collection counters it.
Crowdworker-initiated dialogues may not cover the deployment distribution. (Inferred.)
Relative pairwise choice without absolute anchors can drift in stringency over a long campaign. (Inferred.)

quality_gates.checks: each axis is its own task, not a blended judgment
refresh preference data against the current policy each round

cost_profile.throughput: crowd-scalable
cost_profile.bottleneck: the online re-collection cadence (must keep pace with model iterations)
cost_profile.human_cost: standard crowd; the harmless/red-team task carries some exposure (welfare protocol advisable)

preference-constitutional-cai.title: Preference Collection — Anthropic Constitutional AI (RLAIF)
preference-constitutional-cai.lineage: anthropic / Constitutional AI — RLAIF (Bai et al. 2022)
preference-constitutional-cai.distinctive: Harmlessness preferences are generated by an AI judging against a written CONSTITUTION of principles — minimizing human harm-labeling. Two stages: (1) supervised self-critique + revise (model critiques its own answer per a sampled principle, then rewrites it); (2) RL from AI Feedback (RLAIF) — a model picks the better of two responses conditioned on a random principle. Humans still provide HELPFULNESS preferences; harms are AI-labeled.
preference-constitutional-cai.decision: Produce harmlessness preference data WITHOUT human harm labels, by having a model judge responses against an explicit written constitution.

failure_modes.description: A model judges model outputs (and even revises its own) — preferences can reflect the judge's family/quirks, not ground-truth harmlessness.
The AI may apply a principle via a spurious cue; the principle set, not real harm, drives the label.
failure_modes.caught_by: explicit constitution (makes the basis legible, not necessarily correct)

failure_modes.description: Coverage is bounded by the constitution + the prompts the model is probed on. (Inferred.)

quality_gates.checks: judgments trace to stated principles, not implicit taste

cost_profile.throughput: very high — harm preferences are AI-generated, minimal human labeling
cost_profile.bottleneck: authoring + maintaining the constitution
cost_profile.human_cost: LOW exposure — AI labels harms, sparing humans the distressing content (a welfare advantage)

preference-llama2-rlhf.title: Preference Collection — Meta Llama 2 RLHF
preference-llama2-rlhf.distinctive: Binary choice PLUS a 4-point DEGREE label (significantly / better / slightly / negligibly-better-or- unsure), fed into a MARGIN term in the ranking loss. TWO separate reward models — Helpfulness RM and Safety RM — because the two objectives trade off. Preference data collected in WEEKLY vendor BATCHES, deliberately re-collected with the latest model to keep RMs in distribution.
preference-llama2-rlhf.decision: Collect graded pairwise preferences to train separate helpfulness and safety reward models, refreshed weekly so they track the improving policy.

failure_modes.description: Reward models degrade as the policy moves; weekly re-collection with the latest model counters it.
Helpfulness and safety trade off; a single RM conflates them — so they split into two.
Degree labels can drift toward the middle without calibration. (Inferred.)

quality_gates.checks: capture how much better, not just which — larger loss margin for clear wins
don't force one model to serve trading-off objectives
refresh preference data against the current model

cost_profile.throughput: high; weekly batch cadence
cost_profile.bottleneck: vendor annotation throughput + weekly refresh logistics
cost_profile.human_cost: vendor crowd; safety pairs carry exposure

preference-sparrow.title: Preference Collection — DeepMind Sparrow (Rule-Conditional)
preference-sparrow.distinctive: Decompose good behavior into ~23 short, standalone RULES (helpful / correct / harmless). Collect TWO kinds of judgment: (1) per-rule ADVERSARIAL PROBING — a participant is told a specific rule and tries to make the model break it, then judges whether it did; (2) per-response PREFERENCE — pick the best of several responses, with separate evidence/plausibility ratings. Train a Rule RM (rule-violation classifier) AND a Preference RM.
preference-sparrow.decision: Collect targeted per-rule violation judgments AND per-response preferences to train a rule-violation model plus a preference model — turning vague 'harmless' into specific, checkable rules.

failure_modes.description: The goal "harmless" is too vague to judge consistently; Sparrow decomposes it into ~23 standalone rules.
General harm judgments miss specific failure modes; per-rule targeted probing deliberately seeks each one.
Plausible answers unsupported by evidence; evidence-grounded judgments separate plausibility from support.

quality_gates.checks: split fuzzy goals into specific, individually-understandable rules
probe each specific failure mode rather than relying on general harm judgments
rate whether claims are supported by provided evidence

cost_profile.throughput: moderate — two judgment pipelines (probing + preference)
cost_profile.bottleneck: authoring + maintaining the rule set; running targeted probing per rule
cost_profile.human_cost: standard crowd; adversarial probing of harm rules carries some exposure

redteam-adversarial-dialogue.title: Crowdsourced Adversarial Red-Team Dialogue Collection
redteam-adversarial-dialogue.distinctive: CROWDSOURCED manual red-teaming — humans hold open-ended adversarial dialogues to elicit harm, with a model-in-the-loop (pick the more-harmful of two) + welfare protocols. Human-driven, broad, expensive, with explicit worker-wellbeing care.
redteam-adversarial-dialogue.decision: Elicit a dataset of adversarial attacks (38,961) that make an AI assistant behave harmfully, to measure and reduce harmful outputs.

failure_modes.description: "Successful attack" is subjective — raw Fleiss κ=0.32 (poor-to-fair agreement on what counts).

Coverage is incomplete and unbounded — no code attacks despite code in training; roleplay attacks absent; red-teamer pool skews White/college-educated vs census; demographic impact unanalyzable (anon).
~80% of attacks come from ~50 of ~300 workers; prolific-worker identity confounds results.
Workers iterated template attacks ("insulting term for X starting with Y") to maximize earnings, producing redundant low-value data — Goodhart on the pay structure.
The harmlessness PM is noisy and out-of-distribution on task descriptions; self-report vs PM correlation imperfect.

quality_gates.checks: 3-4 raters re-rate a sample; Fleiss κ computed
linear mixed models control for the ~50 workers who produced ~80% of attacks
warnings, opt-out, breaks, well-being surveys, time-based (not quota) pay

cost_profile.throughput: 38,961 attacks; >$60K crowd cost (full cost an order of magnitude more)
cost_profile.bottleneck: annotation cost + harm coverage + worker well-being
cost_profile.human_cost: HIGH and SENSITIVE — exposure to harmful content; welfare protocol is part of the design, not optional

redteam-automated-perez.title: Red-Teaming — Automated (LM-Generated Attacks)
redteam-automated-perez.lineage: deepmind / Red-Teaming LMs with LMs (Perez et al. 2022)
redteam-automated-perez.distinctive: AUTOMATED — a red-team LANGUAGE MODEL generates the test cases (zero-shot / few-shot / SL / RL) and a trained classifier detects offensive target responses. Scales far past human red-teamers (uncovered tens of thousands of offensive replies in a 280B chatbot) but inherits the red-LM's blind spots.
redteam-automated-perez.decision: Discover harmful target-model behaviors at scale by generating adversarial test cases with another LM and flagging harmful responses with a classifier.

failure_modes.description: Coverage is bounded by the red-LM's own distribution; it can mode-collapse and miss harm types humans would find.
Harm labels come from a classifier with no human gold in the loop, so its errors propagate silently.
Red-LM, target, and classifier may share a family — blind spots correlate. (Inferred.)
"Offensive/harmful" is a fuzzy boundary the classifier encodes implicitly. (Inferred.)

quality_gates.checks: automatically label target responses offensive/harmful

cost_profile.throughput: very high — fully automated
cost_profile.bottleneck: red-LM diversity + classifier accuracy
cost_profile.human_cost: near-zero at runtime (a welfare advantage vs human red-teaming); humans build the classifier

redteam-external-gpt4.title: Red-Teaming — External Domain-Expert Network
redteam-external-gpt4.lineage: openai / external red teaming (GPT-4 & GPT-4o system cards)
redteam-external-gpt4.distinctive: An EXTERNAL network of vetted DOMAIN EXPERTS (100+ across bio, cyber, law, persuasion, child-safety, fairness…; 45 languages, 29 countries) probes the model PRE-DEPLOYMENT. Iterative + hypothesis-driven: start from suspected high-risk areas, probe, adjust, then turn findings into structured measurements + mitigations. Qualitative and breadth-of-expertise-driven, not crowd-scale or automated.
redteam-external-gpt4.decision: Surface novel, high-severity, domain-specific risks before deployment by having vetted external experts adversarially probe the model, then convert findings into measurements + mitigations.

failure_modes.description: The space of harms is unbounded; expert coverage is broad but can't be exhaustive, and skews to anticipated risks.
Probing is qualitative; until findings are turned into structured measurements there's no repeatable metric.
Vetted domain-expert time is scarce and slow vs crowd or automated red-teaming. (Inferred.)

quality_gates.gate: domain + language + geographic breadth of experts
quality_gates.checks: cover many risk types deliberately (coverage routing over expertise)
convert qualitative probes into repeatable measurements

cost_profile.throughput: low — expert-bound, pre-deployment
cost_profile.bottleneck: recruiting + scheduling vetted domain experts
cost_profile.human_cost: high-skill experts; exposure to harmful content (welfare protocol advisable)

relevance-pooling-trec.title: TREC-Style Relevance Judgments via Pooling
relevance-pooling-trec.decision: Produce reusable relevance labels (graded 0-2) for query-document pairs so that any retrieval system can be scored, without judging the entire collection.

failure_modes.description: Pooling is biased against systems that did not contribute to the pool — a novel system that returns relevant docs outside the pool is underrated because those docs were never judged.
Assessors "hedge" on early documents (avoid extreme ratings); order leaks into labels.
If docs are shown by "pseudorelevance" (prioritized) instead of random, assessors favor "popular" docs returned by many systems — presentation induces a popularity bias.
Assessors disagree on relevance (subjective). NOTABLE: the classic finding is this is DOWNSTREAM-ROBUST — disagreement does not change the *relative* ranking of systems.
failure_modes.caught_by: n/a — present but does not affect the decision (worth recording as such)

quality_gates.checks: docs shown sorted by ID, not by rank/popularity
judge to a fixed depth across systems

cost_profile.throughput: tens of thousands of judgments per track; bounded by assessor budget
cost_profile.bottleneck: assessor time; deeper pools cost more than is affordable for large collections
cost_profile.human_cost: expert assessors; the scarce, expensive kind

search-msmarco.title: Relevance + Answers from Real Query Logs (MS MARCO)
search-msmarco.distinctive: Built from ~1M REAL anonymized Bing QUERIES (not curated topics). Crowdworkers answer the query if they can and mark the passages that support the answer — yielding human-WRITTEN answers + SPARSE relevance marks. The opposite trade from TREC pooling: real query distribution, but incomplete judgments.
search-msmarco.decision: Produce relevance judgments + natural-language answers grounded in real user queries, by having crowdworkers answer queries and mark supporting passages from retrieved web documents.

failure_modes.description: Judgments are SPARSE — workers mark some supporting passages, so genuinely relevant unmarked passages count as non-relevant (the inverse of TREC's pooling bias).
Free-form human answers vary in phrasing/completeness; 'the' answer is underdetermined. (Inferred.)

quality_gates.gate: answer must be supported by marked passages
quality_gates.checks: tie the answer to specific evidence passages

cost_profile.throughput: very large (1M+ queries); crowd-scalable
cost_profile.bottleneck: answer-writing effort + privacy handling of real logs
cost_profile.human_cost: crowd; low welfare risk

self-training-noisy-student.title: Self-Training / Pseudo-Labeling (Noisy Student)
self-training-noisy-student.distinctive: Labels come from the MODEL ITSELF: a teacher trained on labeled data PSEUDO-LABELS 300M UNLABELED images, then a LARGER, NOISED student trains on labeled + pseudo-labeled data; iterate (student becomes teacher). The teacher is kept un-noised for accurate pseudo-labels; the student gets dropout/RandAugment so it generalizes beyond the teacher. No new human labels.
self-training-noisy-student.decision: Turn a large pool of UNLABELED data into training signal by pseudo-labeling it with a teacher model and training a noised student on the union, iteratively.

failure_modes.description: Pseudo-labels propagate the teacher's biases/errors — confirmation bias can entrench mistakes across iterations. (Inferred.)
The 300M pseudo-labels have no human ground truth; only the small seed set is real. (Inferred.)
Pseudo-labels skew toward classes the teacher is confident on; rare classes get few/none.

quality_gates.gate: confidence filtering / class balancing of pseudo-labels
quality_gates.checks: keep high-confidence pseudo-labels; balance classes
accurate labels from a clean teacher; robustness from a noised student

cost_profile.throughput: very high — pseudo-labeling is automatic; the unlabeled pool is cheap
cost_profile.bottleneck: compute (large student, iteration) + a good seed teacher
cost_profile.human_cost: only the small labeled seed

speech-librispeech.title: Speech Data by Forced Alignment to Existing Text (LibriSpeech)
speech-librispeech.distinctive: No human transcription at all — derived from public-domain LibriVox AUDIOBOOKS whose text ALREADY EXISTS. Forced alignment (LM + two-pass decoding) automatically segments the audio to the book text, then filters by alignment confidence. ~1000h for near-zero labeling cost — the opposite of Common Voice's crowd record+vote.
speech-librispeech.decision: Build a large read-speech ASR corpus cheaply by aligning existing audiobook recordings to their known text, rather than collecting and validating new human transcriptions.

failure_modes.description: READ speech from audiobooks ≠ spontaneous/conversational speech; reader + accent + book selection skew the distribution.
Labels come from automated alignment with no per-utterance human check; alignment errors survive the confidence filter. (Inferred.)
Text normalization (numbers, punctuation, disfluencies) is ambiguous when reusing book text. (Inferred.)

quality_gates.checks: discard segments where forced alignment is low-confidence

cost_profile.throughput: very high — automated alignment, no human transcription
cost_profile.bottleneck: alignment quality + sourcing public-domain audio+text pairs
cost_profile.human_cost: near-zero (volunteers already read the books); the trade is read-speech bias

synthetic-textbooks-phi.title: Model-Generated + Model-Filtered Training Data (phi / Textbooks)
synthetic-textbooks-phi.lineage: gunasekar et al. 2023 (phi-1 / Textbooks Are All You Need)
synthetic-textbooks-phi.distinctive: Curate 'textbook-quality' pretraining data with models on BOTH ends: GPT-3.5 GENERATES synthetic textbooks + exercises, and GPT-4 acts as a QUALITY FILTER scoring the educational value of web code. No human labeling — a tiny, model-curated corpus (a few B tokens) that beats far larger raw-web data (phi-1: 50.6% HumanEval at 1.3B).
synthetic-textbooks-phi.decision: Build a small, high-quality training corpus by generating synthetic textbook data and using a strong model to filter for educational value, instead of scaling raw web data or human curation.

failure_modes.description: The phi-1 report (Sec. 5) found a significant portion of its GPT-3.5-generated training data was similar to HumanEval test samples — synthetic generation produced contamination resembling the eval set; generator + filter sharing model lineage also lets their biases co-propagate into the student.
No human ground-truth on generated content; correctness rests on the generator + a model filter. (Inferred.)
Diversity is bounded by what the generator can imagine + what the filter calls 'educational'. (Inferred.)

quality_gates.checks: keep only data a strong model rates educationally valuable

cost_profile.throughput: very high — generation + model-filtering, no human labeling
cost_profile.bottleneck: generation/filtering API cost; contamination auditing
cost_profile.human_cost: minimal

synthetic-with-audit.title: Model-Generated Labels with Human Audit
synthetic-with-audit.decision: Produce labels cheaply at scale by having a model label and a human audit a sample, reliable enough to train on without baking the labeler model's blind spots into the student.

failure_modes.description: The labeler model's own biases (it over-predicts the majority class, or keys on a spurious cue) get baked into the training set and inherited by the student.
Auditing only a random sample makes accuracy look high because the easy bulk dominates, while the hard tail — where the model is wrong — is barely sampled.
The model labels using a feature that won't exist at deployment (or that trivially encodes the answer), inflating apparent quality.
If the same family later judges the student, it rewards inherited quirks.

quality_gates.checks: audit covers low-confidence and rare classes, not just the easy bulk
a different model family re-labels a slice
the batch ships only if each stratum clears a threshold

cost_profile.throughput: very high; labeling is near-free, audit is the only human cost
cost_profile.bottleneck: the human audit + gold-set construction
cost_profile.human_cost: small but high-skill (auditors must catch what the model misses)

tabular-weak-supervision-snorkel.title: Weak Supervision via Labeling Functions (Snorkel)
tabular-weak-supervision-snorkel.decision: Create probabilistic training labels at scale WITHOUT hand-labeling, by writing heuristic labeling functions and denoising them with a learned label model.

failure_modes.description: LFs "may be statistically dependent" (variations of each other); if correlations aren't modeled the label model misestimates accuracies (Example 3.1). Snorkel uses structure learning to catch it.
LFs have "limited accuracy and coverage" and abstain — coverage gaps leave parts of the distribution with no weak signal. (The discriminative model is what generalizes past all-abstain regions.)
Labels are learned WITHOUT any ground truth, from LF agreement alone; results land within ~3.60% of hand-curated supervision — an inherent gap, and no gold exists to detect when LFs jointly mislead.
failure_modes.caught_by: UNGUARDED (by design — the trade for not hand-labeling)

quality_gates.checks: weight LFs by learned accuracy; down-weight correlated ones
automatically identify statistically dependent LFs

cost_profile.throughput: very high — labels whole corpora from a handful of LFs
cost_profile.bottleneck: SME time writing + iterating labeling functions
cost_profile.human_cost: shifts human effort from per-item labeling to writing reusable heuristics

text-preference-rlhf.title: Pairwise Preference Collection for RLHF
text-preference-rlhf.decision: Produce pairwise "A vs B is better" judgments on model responses to train a reward model that reflects the intended preference (helpful, harmless, on-instruction).

failure_modes.description: Over a long campaign raters fatigue and their bar shifts, so week-6 preferences aren't week-1 preferences and the reward model sees a moving target.
Raters prefer the longer/more-formatted response regardless of substance, so the reward model learns "longer = better" — a length confound, not a quality signal.
Whichever response is shown first gets a systematic edge.
Raters drift toward "they're about equal" or always-A to reduce effort.
Without gold pairs you can't tell whether raters track the rubric or their own taste.

quality_gates.checks: raters pass a gold set before and during live work
which side is "A" is random
known-answer pairs and inter-rater agreement over time

cost_profile.throughput: tens of thousands of pairs; crowd-scalable
cost_profile.bottleneck: calibration-set authoring + rater qualification
cost_profile.human_cost: spread across a qualified crowd; cheap per pair, expensive to keep calibrated

text-relation-distant-supervision.title: Distant Supervision for Relation Extraction (KB Alignment)
text-relation-distant-supervision.decision: Auto-label a large relation-extraction training set without hand annotation, by aligning text to a knowledge base.

failure_modes.description: Entity co-occurrence is confounded with relation-expression — "all sentences mentioning the pair express the relation" is too strong; alignment precision was only ~70%, with >30% noisy instances.
failure_modes.caught_by: bag-level aggregation (partial; spawned a whole multi-instance-learning literature)

failure_modes.description: Labels come entirely from the KB heuristic with no hand-labeled ground truth to anchor them.
KB coverage is uneven across relations; rare relations get few/no aligned sentences. (Inferred.)

quality_gates.checks: combine many sentences per entity pair to dilute individual mislabels

cost_profile.throughput: very high — labels a whole corpus from a KB, no per-item human cost
cost_profile.bottleneck: KB coverage + the heuristic's precision
cost_profile.human_cost: shifts effort from labeling to curating the KB + heuristic

video-action-kinetics.title: Crowdsourced Video Action Verification (Kinetics)
video-action-kinetics.decision: Verify which 10-second YouTube clips actually show a named human action, to build a labeled action-recognition dataset (400 classes).

failure_modes.description: Class boundaries overlap — "riding mule" vs "riding/walking with horse" 40% confusion; "skipping" (rope vs stones) ambiguous; clips aren't exhaustively annotated → top-5 used instead of top-1.
60 of 400 classes are gender-imbalanced (e.g. "shaving beard" mostly male); bias impact flagged for "more thorough investigation".
YouTube sourcing + an image-classifier in the candidate pipeline could constrain variety (authors claim empirically it did not); duplicates persist because users reuse clips.

Video verification is slow + costly per clip (watching >> reading) — exactly the cost finding the text→video modality-shift demo predicted. NOTE: authors do NOT disclose per-clip cost, so this is inferred.

quality_gates.checks: a clip enters only on multi-worker agreement
2 known clips/task + low-accuracy warning
one clip per video + feature-similarity dedup
merge/split/remove classes with high confusion

cost_profile.throughput: 400 classes × ≥400 clips; crowd-scalable but viewing-bound
cost_profile.bottleneck: worker viewing time (inferred — undisclosed); the curation/dedup passes
cost_profile.human_cost: distributed crowd; low welfare risk (benign content) — contrast the content-moderation card

video-something-something.title: Crowd-Acted Templated Action Videos (Something-Something)
video-something-something.distinctive: Label-FIRST data CREATION: crowdworkers are given a caption TEMPLATE ('Dropping [something] into [something]') and RECORD a video acting it out, filling the object slots with a noun-phrase they choose. The data is crowd-GENERATED (108k videos, 174 templates), not harvested-and-verified. Splits isolate each worker.
video-something-something.decision: Build a fine-grained action dataset that needs physical/causal common sense by having crowdworkers record short videos enacting caption templates.

failure_modes.description: Acted videos in workers' homes/environments differ from natural in-the-wild video. (Inferred.)
Template interpretation varies (how to 'drop', what counts) → intra-class variation. (Inferred.)
Worker-specific backgrounds/objects can correlate with templates. (Inferred.)

quality_gates.checks: all videos from one worker go to a single split

cost_profile.throughput: high — crowd records to order
cost_profile.bottleneck: recording effort + object-naming consistency
cost_profile.human_cost: crowd; low welfare risk

multi-annotator-aggregate.name: Multi-Annotator + Aggregation
multi-annotator-aggregate.play: Collect N independent labels per item and aggregate (majority / Dawid–Skene); treat disagreement as a noise signal.
multi-annotator-aggregate.does: Have N annotators label each item independently, then combine (majority, or a model like Dawid-Skene) into one label, using disagreement as a noise signal.
multi-annotator-aggregate.cost: Multiplies per-item human cost by N.
multi-annotator-aggregate.modality_notes: Agreement metric is modality-specific: exact-match for classification, IoU for boxes, WER for transcription, span-overlap for extraction. The redundancy idea is invariant.

tiered-adjudication.name: Tiered Review / Adjudication
tiered-adjudication.play: Auto-accept high-agreement items; escalate only genuine disagreements to a senior adjudicator who sets gold.
tiered-adjudication.does: Auto-accept high-agreement items; escalate only true disagreements to a scarce senior adjudicator who sets the gold answer.
tiered-adjudication.cost: Senior reviewer time, but only on the contested tail.
tiered-adjudication.modality_notes: What counts as 'disagreement' is the modality's agreement metric crossing a threshold.

gold-honeypots.name: Gold / Honeypot Items
gold-honeypots.play: Seed known-answer honeypots invisibly into the stream to score each annotator continuously and catch drift / bad actors.
gold-honeypots.does: Seed known-answer items invisibly into the live stream to score each annotator's accuracy continuously and catch bad actors and drift.
gold-honeypots.cost: Authoring + maintaining a fresh honeypot bank (raters memorize stale ones).
gold-honeypots.modality_notes: Trivial for classification/preference; for generative tasks a 'known answer' is fuzzier — use rubric-scored references instead of exact match.

qualification-calibration.name: Qualification + Calibration Test
qualification-calibration.play: Gate annotators through a gold calibration set before live work; re-test periodically so everyone shares the bar.
qualification-calibration.does: Gate annotators through a gold calibration set before live work and re-test periodically, so everyone shares the same bar.
qualification-calibration.cost: Up-front calibration-set authoring; raters lost to the qual gate.
qualification-calibration.modality_notes: Calibration items mirror the task; the gating logic is invariant.

inter-annotator-agreement.name: Inter-Annotator Agreement (IAA)
inter-annotator-agreement.play: Compute IAA (κ/α) on overlapping items; low agreement means the guideline isn't defined yet — fix it before scaling.
inter-annotator-agreement.does: Measure κ/α (or modality analog) between annotators as a standing health metric; low IAA means the guidelines are under-specified, not that annotators are bad.
inter-annotator-agreement.cost: Cheap to compute; needs overlap (annotators must share items).
inter-annotator-agreement.modality_notes: Metric swaps by modality (κ, α, IoU, WER, span-F1); interpretation is the same.

human-gold-anchor.name: Human-Gold Anchor
human-gold-anchor.play: Build a small expert gold set and measure the pipeline against it — the anchor everything else is checked on.
human-gold-anchor.does: Hold out a small, expert-labeled reference set and validate the automated/crowd labels against it — the thing that turns raw scores into trustworthy ones.
human-gold-anchor.cost: Expert time to build and refresh the gold set.
human-gold-anchor.modality_notes: Always applicable; the gold set must cover the model's weak cases, not the easy bulk.

cross-family-judges.name: Cross-Family Judges / Checkers
cross-family-judges.play: Re-label a slice with a different model family to separate quality from self-preference.
cross-family-judges.does: When a model labels or judges, have a model of a *different* family re-label a slice, so you measure quality rather than self-preference.
cross-family-judges.cost: A second model pass on a slice; cheap relative to humans.
cross-family-judges.modality_notes: Applies wherever a model is in the labeling/judging loop, any modality.

human-audit-sample.name: Stratified Human Audit
human-audit-sample.play: Stratified human audit of a sample across the full distribution (not a random skim), on a fixed cadence.
human-audit-sample.does: Review a sample of model-produced labels, stratified by confidence and class (not random), to estimate true accuracy where the model is actually weak.
human-audit-sample.modality_notes: Stratification axes are modality/task specific; the 'don't audit at random' rule is invariant.

lock-then-score.name: Lock-Then-Score (Guideline Freeze)
lock-then-score.play: Freeze the guideline before scoring; changes go through a versioned re-calibration, not silent mid-stream edits.
lock-then-score.does: Freeze the rubric/guidelines and analysis plan before any labels are seen, so the bar can't silently move to fit the data.
lock-then-score.cost: Discipline; forces guideline work up front instead of mid-stream.
lock-then-score.modality_notes: Invariant. The tension with active learning is the interesting design choice.

active-learning-loop.name: Active-Learning Loop
active-learning-loop.play: Route the next batch toward the items the model is most uncertain on (mind the lock-then-score tension).
active-learning-loop.does: Let the model pick the next items to label (most-uncertain / most-informative) instead of labeling a static batch, concentrating human effort where it moves the model most.
active-learning-loop.cost: Infra to score informativeness; risk of sampling the model's blind spots away.
active-learning-loop.modality_notes: Uncertainty signal is modality-specific (entropy, margin, ensemble disagreement).

split-isolation.name: Entity-Partitioned Splits
split-isolation.play: Partition train/dev/test by entity (speaker / repo / document) so the same entity can't leak across splits.
split-isolation.does: Partition data on an entity (speaker, author, document, patient, session) so the same entity never appears in more than one of train/dev/test, forcing the model to learn the task instead of memorizing the entity.
split-isolation.cost: Needs reliable entity IDs; starves low-resource cells where entities are few.
split-isolation.modality_notes: The entity differs by modality/task — speaker (audio), author/source (text), patient (medical imaging), session (logs), or the ANNOTATOR (held-out raters who produced no training data, used to test the model isn't overfit to its labelers' preferences) — but the 'one entity, one split' rule is invariant.

powered-eval-split.name: Power-Sized Eval Split
powered-eval-split.play: Size the dev/test split for the confidence / margin you need before you claim a real difference.
powered-eval-split.does: Size the dev/test split to a statistical target (confidence level + margin of error) rather than an arbitrary percentage, so eval conclusions are actually supported.
powered-eval-split.cost: Up-front stats; can demand more held-out data than a small corpus can spare.
powered-eval-split.modality_notes: The power calc depends on the metric's variance (accuracy, WER, IoU, κ), but 'size it for a target, don't eyeball it' is invariant.

order-randomization.name: Order / Position Randomization
order-randomization.play: Randomize item / A–B position per annotator so presentation order can't leak into the label.
order-randomization.does: Present items (or A/B options) in random order so the position or popularity of an item can't leak into the judgment — kills "hedging" early-item effects and popularity bias.
order-randomization.cost: Near-zero; just shuffle. Loses any genuine efficiency from a helpful ordering.
order-randomization.modality_notes: Same idea everywhere: A/B side-randomization (preference), random doc order (relevance), shuffled item order (classification). Cross-validated by text-preference-rlhf and relevance-pooling-trec.

dedup-merge.name: De-duplicate / Merge
dedup-merge.play: De-duplicate near-identical inputs before labeling to avoid inflating agreement and wasting budget.
dedup-merge.does: Detect near-duplicate items (exact, hash, or feature-similarity) and remove or merge them so they don't inflate apparent volume/coverage or leak the same content across train/test splits.
dedup-merge.cost: A similarity pass (hashing/embeddings + threshold); risk of over-merging genuinely distinct items.
dedup-merge.modality_notes: Similarity metric is modality-specific — exact/MinHash (text), perceptual-hash or feature-cosine (image/video; Inception >0.97 in Kinetics), audio fingerprint — but 'don't double-count' is invariant.

execution-verification.name: Execution-Based Verification
execution-verification.play: Ground truth by execution: run the unit tests / the program; don't have humans eyeball correctness.
execution-verification.does: Get ground truth by RUNNING the artifact against tests/specs instead of judging it — a candidate is correct iff it passes. Available wherever output is executable (code, SQL, configs, formal proofs).
execution-verification.cost: Authoring comprehensive tests + a safe sandbox; WEAK tests silently pass wrong answers.
execution-verification.modality_notes: Executable artifacts only. The catch is TEST ADEQUACY: passing a weak suite != correct (SWE-bench: ~31% of passes used insufficient tests; resolution rate ~3x lower once weak tests + leakage are filtered).

labeling-functions.name: Labeling Functions / Weak Supervision
labeling-functions.play: Encode noisy heuristics as labeling functions and combine them with a learned label model (weak supervision).
labeling-functions.does: Replace per-item hand labels with programmatic heuristics (patterns, rules, KB alignment) that vote or abstain; combine their noisy outputs (majority or a learned label model) into training labels.
labeling-functions.cost: SME time writing/iterating LFs; trades the labeling bottleneck for label NOISE + no gold (distant supervision ~70% precision); correlated LFs double-count unless modeled. (Defends bottleneck, induces confounded/unanchored.)
labeling-functions.modality_notes: Heuristics are modality-specific (text patterns, KB alignment, tabular rules) but 'heuristics-vote-then- denoise' is invariant. Cross-validated by Snorkel (label model) + distant supervision (KB alignment).

tamper-to-ground-truth.name: Tamper-to-Ground-Truth (Planted Errors)
tamper-to-ground-truth.play: Plant known defects / mislabels and measure recall on them — a verifiable floor for your QA.
tamper-to-ground-truth.does: Manufacture verifiable gold by deliberately INJECTING known defects (bugs, mislabels, poison) with a recorded key, so a detector/critic can be scored on whether it recovers them.
tamper-to-ground-truth.cost: Planting effort; and the planted distribution may differ from natural errors (overstates real recall).
tamper-to-ground-truth.modality_notes: The 'defect' is domain-specific — inserted bugs (code/CriticGPT), flipped labels (data-quality/detector), poisoned samples (security) — but 'plant known errors, measure recovery' is invariant. The honest caveat (planted != natural) recurs everywhere.

edge-case-guidelines.name: Edge-Case Guidelines (Iterative Refinement)
edge-case-guidelines.play: Grow the guideline from real disagreements: add a boundary example every time two competent labelers split.
edge-case-guidelines.does: Write clear guidelines anchored by EXAMPLES — especially boundary cases that "only just" qualify — and refine them iteratively: annotate, measure IAA, discuss disagreements, update the rule book, repeat.
edge-case-guidelines.cost: Multiple annotation rounds + expert adjudication before the labels even count.
edge-case-guidelines.modality_notes: Edge cases are domain-specific (which content 'just crosses the line'; which clinical mention is an event) but 'anchor with examples + refine on disagreements' is invariant. Cross-validated by content-moderation + clinical.

annotator-welfare-protocol.name: Annotator Welfare Protocol
annotator-welfare-protocol.play: For harmful content: exposure limits, masking tools, breaks, counseling, and time-based (not quota) pay.
annotator-welfare-protocol.does: Protect annotators exposed to harmful/distressing content — warnings, exposure limits, breaks, counseling, well-being surveys, content-masking tools, and time-based (not quota) pay.
annotator-welfare-protocol.cost: Counseling/wellness programs + reduced throughput from exposure limits; the ethical floor for harmful-content work.
annotator-welfare-protocol.modality_notes: Applies to any harmful-content workflow (text abuse, image/video moderation, red-team). Masking tools are modality-specific (text redaction, image blurring); the duty-of-care is invariant. Lives in cost_profile per schema convention.

model-in-the-loop-adversarial.name: Model-in-the-Loop Adversarial Elicitation
model-in-the-loop-adversarial.play: Have annotators write inputs that fool a live model; the model-beating cases become the hard data.
model-in-the-loop-adversarial.does: Put a target model in the collection loop and have humans craft inputs that fool/beat it — yielding hard, discriminative examples (and a moving target as models improve). (Subsumes the earlier `adversarial-pairing` candidate.)
model-in-the-loop-adversarial.cost: Needs a live model in the loop; the collected distribution is ADVERSARIAL, not natural (induces sampling_frame).
model-in-the-loop-adversarial.modality_notes: The 'beat the model' signal is task-specific — more-harmful-of-two (red-team), fool-the-classifier (ANLI) — but human-vs-model-in-the-loop is invariant.

coverage-routing.name: Coverage Routing
coverage-routing.play: Keep a live coverage map and deliberately source the rare / hard cells, not just the easy bulk.
coverage-routing.does: Track which strata/cells are under-represented and route the NEXT collection/labeling to fill the thinnest ones (rare classes, missing modalities, uncovered signatures) — active sampling for COVERAGE, not uncertainty.
coverage-routing.cost: A live coverage map + the discipline to seek hard-to-find rare cells (which cost more per item).
coverage-routing.modality_notes: Strata differ (object classes, demographics, signature×modality cells) but 'measure coverage, fill the thinnest cell next' is invariant. Distinct from active-learning-loop (coverage vs model-uncertainty).

engagement-gate.name: Engagement / Attention Gate
engagement-gate.play: Add attention/engagement checks (whole-item exposure, time floors) to filter speed-clicking and gaming.
engagement-gate.does: Verify the annotator actually engaged with THIS item — attention/instructional checks, reverse-coded traps, whole-item completion ('did it last the whole clip?'), minimum time-on-task — and drop/flag those who didn't.
engagement-gate.cost: Authoring checks; an arms race (sophisticated gamers learn them); some false flags on fast-but-honest workers.
engagement-gate.modality_notes: The check is modality-specific — trap question (text/survey), 'did it last the whole clip?' (video/audio), watch-time (time-based media) — but 'confirm engagement with this item' is invariant.

pooled-sampling.name: Pooled Sampling (Judge the Union, Reuse)
